name: quantum_circuit_computing

name: measurement_based_quantum_computing

name: quantum_walks
evidence: quantum walks spread ballistically and are universal for quantum computation on graphs built for the circuit (cite:childs-2009; cite:childs-2013); under the bare beat U a lone vibe is an exact coined walk on its line, the same bytes on the flat control (E-CMP-0037; E-CMP-0017), and it never leaves that line, so it searches nothing: the marked dock holds at most (1 + 2R)/N and the oracle stays below the oracle-free peak (E-CMP-0039); an exact Grover walk, a different rule, beats no classical baseline once every cost is counted (E-CMP-0047); universal walk computation needs the laid-out meetings of row 151 (E-CMP-0040), and the route with the program in the initial state alone is open; if amplitudes count as added structure rather than base, they join it

evidence: slow Hamiltonian evolution is polynomially equivalent to the circuit model (cite:aharonov-2007); the bare beat U is one fixed beat with no slowly varying Hamiltonian, so the adiabatic path itself is not realized, and this row's power is reached only as a circuit of laid-out meetings, row 151 (E-CMP-0033; E-CMP-0040); if amplitudes count as added structure rather than base, they join it

name: infinite_time_turing_machines
evidence: infinite-time machines run through transfinite ordinal stages and take a limit of each cell at limit stages (cite:hamkins-2000); physically this needs a completed infinite run that someone then reads, a supertask, which contradicts base:finite_steps, since the mesh takes one beat per step and never finishes an infinite run

name: accelerating_turing_machines
evidence: an accelerating machine takes each step in half the time of the last, so infinitely many steps fit in two time units (cite:copeland-2002); physically this needs no smallest duration and no bound on signal speed or energy per step, which contradicts base:finite_steps, since every mesh step is one beat and a difference crosses at most a fixed number of hops per beat

name: zeno_machines
evidence: a Zeno machine finishes infinitely many operations in finite time by geometric acceleration (cite:potgieter-2006); it needs time divisible without bound with each shorter operation still completing, which a fixed discrete beat contradicts (base:finite_steps)

name: infinite_register_machines
evidence: infinite-time register machines run for ordinal time and set each register at a limit stage from its earlier values (cite:koepke-2006); physically they need unbounded registers, which the mesh can hold only as particle separations, and completed transfinite runs, which contradict base:finite_steps

name: ordinal_turing_machines
evidence: ordinal machines have a tape of every ordinal length and run for ordinal time, computing exactly the constructible sets (cite:koepke-2005); physically they need a transfinite tape and supertasks, while the mesh has countably many docks and one beat per step (base:finite_steps)

name: persistent_turing_machines
evidence: a persistent machine keeps its work tape between interactions with an environment (cite:goldin-2004) and goes beyond a function only through that environment, so its one physical assumption is an outside source of input, which the open ball's boundary gives; the machine itself is the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: interactive_machines
evidence: interactive machines receive and emit an unending stream (cite:wegner-1997; cite:van-leeuwen-2001); they need no physical assumption beyond an environment that keeps supplying input, and exceed Turing power only if that environment is itself noncomputable; the open ball exchanges with its outside at its boundary and the machine is the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: inductive_turing_machines
evidence: an inductive machine's result is the value its output finally stops changing at (cite:burgin-2005), which reaches exactly the limit-computable sets (cite:gold-1965); it needs no supertask, only a run without end, but no observer can know at any finite beat that the output is final; a closed reversible box only cycles, so a settling output needs the open ball's sink or a kept history, and the machine is the row 1 simulation (cite:margolus-1984; cite:bennett-1973)

name: super_recursive_algorithms
evidence: an umbrella for models whose results go beyond the recursive functions (cite:burgin-2005): its limit and interactive members need no physical assumption beyond an unending run or an outside input (rows 222 to 224), while its supertask members need infinitely many steps in finite time (rows 217 to 221), so the class as a whole has no single verdict

name: relativistic_hypercomputers
evidence: a computer on a worldline of infinite proper time signals an observer whose own proper time stays finite, possible only in a Malament-Hogarth spacetime such as near a rotating black hole (cite:hogarth-1992; cite:etesi-2002); it needs that spacetime, a computer stable forever and reception of an unboundedly blueshifted signal; on the mesh a difference moves at most a fixed number of hops per beat, so a finite stretch of any observer's beats has finitely many dock-beats in its past and never sees an infinite run (base:finite_steps)

name: infinite_precision_analog_computers
evidence: analog machines and recurrent networks with exact real numbers compute nonuniform classes beyond the Turing limit (cite:siegelmann-1995; cite:blum-1989); they need storing, adding and comparing exact reals with no noise floor, which contradicts base:discrete_state; with finitely many digits they are ordinary computers
